claim: In a study with 280 participants, using LLMs (free prompting, direct generation, or a reframing-theory structured method) did not improve the quality of problem frames.
quote: We found that using LLMs does not help improve the quality of problem frames.
authors: Joongi Shin, Anna Polyanskaya, Andres Lucero, Antti Oulasvirta
title: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing
transfer: Do not assume an LLM reframing step helps; run it only as an A/B arm at equal tokens on open tasks and measure frame quality.

claim: The same study found LLM use widened the gap between experienced and inexperienced designers and lowered perceived agency of less experienced participants.
title: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing
transfer: none directly; a warning that frame quality depends on the user, so do not expect a novice-to-expert lift from a reframing step.

claim: LLM design agents get stuck on familiar solutions like human designers; a self-regulation loop and a separate co-regulation agent both beat a baseline loop on a battery pack design problem at no substantially higher compute, co-regulation best.
authors: Zeda Xu, Nikolas Martelaro, Christopher McComb
title: Supervising Ralph Wiggum: Exploring a Metacognitive Co-Regulation Agentic AI Loop for Engineering Design
transfer: On open routes, a separate call reads the trace every 2 to 3 steps and names an unexplored region; test against self-monitoring at equal tokens.

claim: Generative AI shows design fixation. In a study with 10 designers making office chairs (96 GenAI solutions vs 105 Red Dot entries), ChatGPT text showed repetition, high-frequency words and lower novelty (67.4% vs 78.2%).
authors: Liuqing Chen, Yaxuan Song, Chunyuan Zheng, Qianzhi Jing, Preben Hansen, Lingyun Sun
title: Understanding Design Fixation in Generative AI
transfer: Measure fixation in our agent as repeated themes and high-frequency terms across candidates; use as a diversity metric.

claim: The same paper lists mitigations: non-routine knowledge bases, multi-agent collaboration, analogies, showing examples without direct answers, adjustable randomness. These are proposals, not tested.
title: Understanding Design Fixation in Generative AI
transfer: Candidate arms: analogy from a distant domain, higher temperature, a second agent.

claim: In that study less experienced participants adopted AI output directly while experienced designers assessed it critically.
title: Understanding Design Fixation in Generative AI
transfer: The agent plays the novice who adopts its first output, so it needs its own critic step on open routes.

claim: ChatGPT-4 acted as an inventor in a 48-hour hackathon against graduate students (over 100 prototypes); its team placed second of six. It had strong concept generation but abandoned promising ideas after minor difficulties, added complexity, and showed design fixation.
quote: The LLM's concept generation capabilities were particularly strong.
authors: Daniel Nygard Ege, Henrik Ovrebo, Vegar Stubberud, Martin Berg, Christer Elverum, Martin Steinert, Havard Vestad
title: ChatGPT as an inventor: Eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
transfer: Add a persistence rule: do not drop a promising idea after one failed check; require a diagnosis of the failure first.

claim: Zero-shot chain-of-thought prompts built on Dorst and Cross problem-driven vs solution-driven styles made LLMs match human styles on static features and give more novel, complete solutions than baselines, but not the nonlinear problem-solution transitions of humans.
authors: Xiyuan Zhang, Jinyu Gu, Hongliang Chen, Shiying Ding, Chunlei Chai, Hao Fan
title: Leveraging LLMs to emulate the design processes of different cognitive styles
transfer: A fixed program should supply the problem-solution switching itself, since the model does not do it in one pass (supports a capped bridge cycle).

claim: Curated reasoning in DesignerlyLoop (users inspect, reorganize and selectively regenerate LLM reasoning) improved design quality and creativity in a 20-designer study, after a formative study with 8 designers.
authors: Anqi Wang, Zhengyi Li, Xin Tong, Pan Hui
title: DesignerlyLoop: Forming Design Intent through Curated Reasoning for Human-LLM Alignment
transfer: Keep intent separate from reasoning and allow regenerating one reasoning step; human-in-loop result, so transfer is partial.

claim: GPT-4o scored lower on soundness (about 0.30) than human designer groups (about 0.45) on latent need elicitation; prompting with guidance from the human protocol raised explicit annotation use but gave the lowest variance and did not broaden ideas.
authors: Ryan Bruggeman, Estefania Ciliotta Chehade, Tucker Marion, Paolo Ciuccarelli
title: Probabilistic Methods for Evaluating Human and LLMs During Design Problem-Solving
venue: Proceedings of the Design Society vol 5 (ICED25), 2651-2660
n: 5 designers per protocol group, 30 workshop, 43 survey
transfer: Copying expert steps into the prompt narrowed output. Do not prompt expert steps alone; add a diversity forcing step.

claim: In the same study LLM outputs mostly restated surface product attributes, and GPT-4o outputs clustered mid-range while humans covered both obvious and highly latent needs. Authors call the human samples small and results exploratory.
title: Probabilistic Methods for Evaluating Human and LLMs During Design Problem-Solving
transfer: Use soundness and completeness as scoring ideas for agent traces; add a 'what would the user not say' step.

claim: Wadinambiarachchi et al. report that using an AI image generator in ideation raised fixation on an initial example and gave fewer ideas, less variety and lower originality than baseline.
title: The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking
transfer: Human-side evidence that AI examples cause fixation; supports generating before showing any draft or memory lesson. Page returned 403; known from a search summary only.

claim: Kruger and Cross found four strategies in nine designers (problem-driven, solution-driven, information-driven, knowledge-driven), and strategy was not simply related to solution quality.
title: Solution driven versus problem driven design: strategies and outcomes
transfer: Do not hard-code 'analyze problem first'. Re-fetch returned 403, so this rests on the earlier brief.

claim: Dorst and Cross 2001 studied nine experienced designers and reported problem-solution co-evolution; not re-verified this session.
title: Creativity in the design process: co-evolution of problem-solution
transfer: Bridge step capped at 2 cycles; keep as hypothesis until tested in an LLM at equal tokens.

claim: ICCC 2026 paper 78 (LLM reframing; earlier brief says 7 students rated 27 answers over three prompting strategies) could not be read this session because the PDF fetch returned binary.
title: ICCC 2026 paper 78
